newsitem.title: UK: London gold eyes support at $338, platinum down.
newsitem.headline: London gold eyes support at $338, platinum down.

text.p: Gold prices eased on Wednesday and were looking to test critical support at $338 an ounce following a report saying central banks might sell gold to raise money.
Bullion fixed just easier at $340.70 from $341.60 previously. By 1030 GMT spot gold was indicated at $340.80/$341.10 after Tuesday's close of $341.40/1.90.
Andy Smith, analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), said central banks were likely to consider several ways of activating their gold reserves. But not all options would wreck the price.
The markets were right to fear gold sales from European central banks in particular to qualify for a single currency, he said in a study.
"People were marking prices down on the back of UBS comments," said a dealer. "The trend seems to be down anyway because the bounce from $338 (last week) was pretty poor.
"If gold breaks $338, we can see $332 easily because everyone thinks that $338 will be the low."
Aside from rallies in U.S. stocks and the dollar, negative sentiment also spilled over from an easier platinum market, which had spearheaded the precious metals rally that began last Thursday.
"There is a worry that the platinum thing is a one big spoof and that it will come off," said the London dealer.
Platinum shed $2.50 to $375.00 an ounce on follow-through selling from New York on Tuesday.
Although platinum has eased significantly from its high of $382.50 last week, volatility was expected to continue amid protracted delays in Russia's platinum group metals (PGM) sales.
"With lease rates as high as 10 percent (for one month), I'm still bullish about it," said another dealer.
Russian central bank officials were in talks with Japanese trade houses this week about its future role as a PGM seller.

The apparent power struggle between the Russian precious metals export agency Almaz and the central bank is keeping the market in suspense. PGM exports have stalled since December and no agreement is in sight for sales to leading buyer Japan.
"There are so many stories, who knows. But I think Almaz are expecting to be the agents," said a dealer.
Palladium attracted borrowing activity, with one-month lease rates still quoted as high as 14 percent. Spot palladium was at $155.25/$156.25, up $1.00.
Silver came down three cents in tandem with gold to $4.72/$4.74, but it seemed to be less bearish.
"I would be surprised if $4.65-70 broke at the moment. Silver has got very little interest," said a dealer.
